text:
sophie: Quick async check-in — what I did / blockers / today
what I did: rolled priority-based routing canary (20%) for a subset of /v1 routes, bumped route_priority for embedding endpoints to prefer cold-paths to save cost
blocker: staging showed a ~2% bump in 429s between 10:23–10:35 UTC; not sure if batching change or route bucketing interaction
today: narrow canary to 5%, enable per-request bucket logging, and watch 15m windows; will rollback if sustained 429 > 1.5%

max: Can you paste the canary config and the exact canary id? also are those 429s originating from dedicated pools or shared pools? @anika did we touch global quotas?

sophie: sure — canary id: prio-canary-20240425. config snippet:```json
{
  "id": "prio-canary-20240425",
  "traffic_percent": 20,
  "route_selector": {"path_prefix": "/v1/embed"},
  "overrides": {"route_priority": "prefer_cold"}
}```
429s look like they hit the rate-limiter, not auth.

anika: I didn't change quotas. I landed the batching TTL tweak last night on staging (only), could be KV cache TTL + new priority path causing token distribution shifts. I'll look at the staging deploys around that window.

li: I can add a short-lived dashboard for per-route token distribution + rate-bucket id. Want me to patch dashboards and set an alert at 1% 429?

kai: FYI auth rotated a signing key yesterday but we have fallback keys; that would show 401s not 429s. I checked and auth errors are flat.

sophie: logs confirm 401s stable; 429s concentrated on embed routes. infra-bot: can you run a quick sweep for hot buckets on staging during that window?

infra-bot: scan complete — hotspots detected: rate_bucket_42 and rate_bucket_73 had brief bursts. No host-level CPU or OOMs.

max: If you need a fast rollback command: `./tools/routectl set-canary prio-canary-20240425 0` — tested locally.

sophie: thanks — planning to drop to 5% at 10:45 and enable detailed bucket logging. Will update in ~30m. /cc @li @anika

anika: :thumbsup: I'll stand by and follow logs with you.

li: on it — adding the metric now, ETA ~15m.

deploy-bot: notice: canary deploy prio-canary-20240425 completed at 2024-04-25T10:20:00Z -> 20% traffic.

sophie: follow-up: after narrowing and additional logging we still reproduced the small 429 spike, so rolled back at ~11:07. After rollback, 429s returned to baseline. Immediate action items: correlate batching windows with bucket assignment, and add a canary-ramp guard to abort on 429 > 1% for 5m. I'll open an RFC and small PR for the guard script.

max: nice find, thanks for the quick rollback. no blockers from me.

kai: great incident handling. If you want I can double-check signing-key logs, but seems unrelated.

sophie: rolled back and closing loop — will post RFC and drop the postmortem notes in #postmortems once I have timings. Thanks everyone for quick help.
